items.name: chat.append_artifact
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.1 · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0
items.summary: Attach a structured artifact to the conversation that hosts this App window. The handler normalises the caller's `artifact` object, stamps it with the server `ts` and `window_uuid`, and broadcasts an `artifact_appended` event over the window's event channel so the chat surface (and any other tab on the same session) can render it. This is the ONE fully-implemented chat method.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — `X-Anna-App-Token` minted by `window.create`.

items.signature: anna.chat.append_artifact(args: {artifact: {kind?: string, app_slug?: string, summary?: string, payload_ref?: string, data?: unknown}}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{artifact_id: string}>

params.name: artifact
params.summary: The artifact payload. `invalid_arg` if not an object. Every field below is optional; unknown fields are dropped (the handler only copies the five named keys).

params.name: artifact.kind
params.summary: Free-form category tag. Coerced to string and **truncated to 40 chars**. Defaults to `app_event`.

params.name: artifact.app_slug
params.summary: Optional app slug for attribution. Passed through verbatim (no validation).

params.name: artifact.summary
params.summary: Human-readable one-liner. Coerced to string and **truncated to 1000 chars**.

params.name: artifact.payload_ref
params.summary: Optional reference (e.g. a `files.*` path or `storage` key) pointing at the full payload. Passed through verbatim.

params.name: artifact.data
params.summary: Optional inline structured data. Passed through as-is — keep it small; there is no server-side size clamp on this field, so prefer `payload_ref` for large blobs.

returns.desc: `artifact_id` is generated server-side as `app-<window_uuid[:8]>-<unix_ts_seconds>`. It is NOT a durable database id — the artifact is delivered as a transient `artifact_appended` event (`{window_uuid, artifact}`), not persisted to a conversation table. Treat the id as a correlation handle for the emitted event, not a primary key you can re-fetch later.

errors.name: invalid_arg
errors.desc: `artifact` is present but not an object.

errors.name: permission_denied
errors.desc: `manifest.ui.host_api.chat` does not list `append_artifact` (or `*`). The dispatch ACL gate (`host_api_allows`) runs before the handler.

limitations: Transient delivery only — the artifact is emitted as an `artifact_appended` event, NOT written to a conversation/message table. A client that wasn't subscribed when the event fired will not see it on reload.
`kind` is truncated to 40 chars and `summary` to 1000 chars; over-long values are silently clipped (no error).
`artifact.data` has no server-side size clamp — for large payloads store the bytes via `files.*` / `storage.*` and pass a `payload_ref` instead of inlining.
ACL gate is `manifest.ui.host_api.chat` (must list `append_artifact` or `*`); `manifest.permissions[]` is display/audit only and is NEVER checked.

items.name: chat.write_message
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.1 · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0 · functional stub (Phase 3)
items.summary: PHASE-3 FUNCTIONAL STUB. Post a message authored by the App into the live conversation. Today the handler ONLY emits a `chat_message_from_app` event ({window_uuid, role, content}) for any subscribed UI to render — it does NOT persist the message to a conversation/message table. The method IS registered (not `_h_not_implemented`), so it returns a `message_id` and does not raise, but durable thread persistence is not yet wired.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — `X-Anna-App-Token` minted by `window.create`.

items.signature: anna.chat.write_message(args: {role?: string, content: string}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{message_id: string}>

params.name: role
params.summary: Author role for the emitted message. Passed through verbatim (no enum validation); defaults to `assistant`.

params.name: content
params.summary: Message text. Coerced to string and **truncated to 4000 chars**. An omitted/empty value emits an empty message rather than erroring.

returns.desc: `message_id` is generated server-side as `msg-<unix_ms>` (milliseconds). Like `append_artifact`, this is a correlation handle for the emitted `chat_message_from_app` event, NOT a durable database id you can re-fetch.

errors.name: permission_denied
errors.desc: `manifest.ui.host_api.chat` does not list `write_message` (or `*`). The dispatch ACL gate runs before the handler.

limitations: FUNCTIONAL STUB (Phase 3): emits a `chat_message_from_app` event but does NOT persist the message. It will not survive a reload and is not part of `chat.read_history` (which is itself unimplemented).
`content` is truncated to 4000 chars; `role` is unvalidated.
ACL gate is `manifest.ui.host_api.chat` (must list `write_message` or `*`); `manifest.permissions[]` is never checked.

items.name: chat.read_history
items.since: Declared in dispatch table · current v0.13.0 / dispatcher 0.17.0 · NOT yet implemented (Phase 3)
items.summary: PHASE-3 STUB — NOT yet implemented. The method is registered in the dispatch table (so the namespace/method name is reserved and ACL-gated), but the handler unconditionally raises `not_implemented`. Do not call it in production flows; there is currently no way to read prior conversation turns from an App bundle.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — `X-Anna-App-Token` minted by `window.create`.

items.signature: anna.chat.read_history(args?: object, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<never>  // always rejects with not_implemented

returns.desc: Never resolves — the handler raises `HostRpcError("not_implemented", "chat.read_history is Phase 3")` before reading any argument. The eventual shape (paginated prior turns scoped to the App's installation) is not yet contracted.

errors.name: permission_denied
errors.desc: `manifest.ui.host_api.chat` does not list `read_history` (or `*`). The ACL gate still runs before the (unimplemented) handler.

limitations: NOT IMPLEMENTED: always raises `not_implemented`. There is no supported way to read conversation history from an App today.
Even though the method is reserved + ACL-gated, granting it in `manifest.ui.host_api.chat` does nothing useful until the Phase-3 implementation lands.
